evidence:
REACHABILITY (all capabilities reachable). (1) Runtime: agent image task/environment/Dockerfile is byte-identical to the template: node:22-bookworm-slim, express@5.1.0 and better-sqlite3@12.4.1 global with NODE_PATH=/usr/local/lib/node_modules; tests/Dockerfile:9,20-21 installs the same. instruction.md:13 'Server dependencies are already available, so don't install packages' is therefore satisfiable; sessions/password checks (node:crypto), live updates (polling/SSE, hireops_rules.md:123 'Polling, server-sent events and sockets are all acceptable'), drafts (browser storage, rules:174 'Where drafts are kept is yours') all need only Node built-ins, Express, SQLite and the browser. The golden imports only express, better-sqlite3 and node built-ins (src/db.js:7, src/index.js:18). (2) Seed: environment/assets/seed_data.json parses and contains everything the brief/rules rely on: 10 users matching instruction.md:17 emails and roles exactly; 3 jobs with recruiter_id, manager_id, interview_limit; 16 applications with stage+position (APP-301 carries rejected_from/reject_reason); 127 messages (APP-101 = 120, the 'long one'); 3 notes; 6 read markers; candidate_status_labels and thread_page_size=30 (rules:208-209). Derived graded facts check out: Lena read_count 2 of APP-301's 3 messages, the third by USR-REC3, so unread=1 as functional/prompt.md:25 states; Noor's 120 messages page 30/30/30/30 with remaining 90->60->30->0. (3) Runtime contract stated and consistent: instruction.md:13-15 and integration.md:3-14 give /app/server.js, port 3000/PORT, /api/health with no DB, /app/app.db/DB_PATH, seed path, copy-into-/app; rules:198-202 state cwd independence, unprivileged writable copy and the exact env set test.sh:139-146 injects (PATH, NODE_PATH, HOME, PORT, DB_PATH). No fixed clock is needed: no graded rule depends on wall-clock time (activity is ordered newest first; 'a moment ago' in instruction.md:3 has no time window). Network is public, so CDN fonts/scripts (instruction.md:13) are reachable and not a defect.

SINGLE READING ON GRADED PATHS. I walked every protocol step (S, M, L, C, B(0)-(14), N, T, U, K, R, V, A, D) against hireops_rules.md and found each expected outcome derivable from the public rules: one-stage moves (rules:47-53), reopen only to rejected-from with reason cleared and restored by undo (rules:51, 96-97), bottom arrival and board order for bulk (rules:57-58, 89-92 -> Y,W,X and A2,V), interview places counted for the set and for undo (rules:63-65, 92, 98), version-based 409 naming who (rules:77-80; instruction.md:3) which makes the ABA replay in protocol C refused under the mandated version reading, undo invalidation by any move/re-order/reject/reopen but not notes, once-only, superseded by a later move (rules:98-100; instruction.md:3 'nobody has touched' is explicitly narrowed by the rule that a note is not a change), manager scope Interview/Offer/Hired plus reject/reopen from Interview/Offer (rules:70-72), 401/403/404 (rules:21-23), unread/seen definitions (rules:151-166), paging (rules:144-147), candidate wording and redaction list (rules:179-194). These are a single reasonable reading.

AMBIGUITIES REPORTED (row requires every one; none rises to an instruction-level Fail):
(a) Interview-full control availability. rules:82-85 describe optimistic move + server refusal + focus kept, but nothing says a move the client already knows is over capacity must still be offered; the functional protocol explicitly makes hiding optional for other refused moves (hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_hired, hro_mgr_other_job) but hro_refused_put_back (judge.toml ~line 132) fails when 'no reason is shown, or focus is not on a control of that card'. A UI that silently omits Interview from the move menu when 2/2 (a defensible 'prevent invalid moves' reading) shows no reason and would score 0 on a weight-2 row; a UI that disables the option with a visible reason likely passes ('A UI that refuses before the card moves ... also passes'). The golden offers adjacency-only options and lets the server refuse (board.js ~145-157, 186-196). Severity P3/P2: the omit-with-no-reason reading is weaker because instruction.md:3 says 'tell me why'.
(b) Activity granularity for multi-card moves. rules:110 'Every ... move ... is recorded ... as a readable line' and rules:96 / instruction.md:3 treat a several-card move as ONE move ('undo my last move, single or several'), so one combined line per bulk move is a reasonable reading; hro_activity and protocol A (prompt.md:49) require 'each card of every multi-card move' to have its line with the stages. A combined line naming each card and stages likely satisfies the judge; a summary line ('Rafael moved 3 candidates to Screen') is plausible under the rules but fails. P3.
(c) Whether a within-stage re-order is itself an undoable 'move' that supersedes the person's earlier move (rules:96-100 list re-order separately from move). Not exercised by any protocol step in a way that changes an expected outcome (B(3) re-order precedes a bulk move; all later undos are refused for other reasons), so ungraded. Note only.
(d) Cross-row grading risk surfaced while checking reachability (owner should route to rows 18/32/37, not decided here): the public rule is clear that a conversation open at its newest message counts as read live (rules:158, 165) and the golden implements it with SSE and ~300 ms refresh (app.js:135,142; threads.js:150-157 markRead on live arrival). Protocol U (prompt.md:41) has Tomas's page open on the conversation when he sends his third message and never tells the judge to close or leave it before 'Rafael then sends a new message: it shows as not seen; Aud opens the conversation: still not seen'. If the judge keeps Tomas's context open (U's last step expects 'his page left open'), a conforming app, including the golden, marks Rafael's message seen within about a second, so hro_seen (weight 1.5) can false-fail. The same open-page lifecycle question affects the expected Mei Lin unread count after she writes in T. Unmeasured: the scripted golden run (results/workspace.json, 'seen only when the other side opens' passed) does not reproduce the judge's context lifecycle, and no configured judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope says full configured grading is absent).

Plausible broken app that could pass this row's concern: none specific to row 6; reachability is not something a weak app can game. Conforming alternatives that could fail: (a), (b) and the (d) context-lifecycle trap above. No unreachable item found. Risk stays true because (d) is unmeasured and (a)/(b) are unresolved ambiguities; no Oracle, model or portal score is claimed.
counterexample: (a) A conforming app hides the 'Interview' option for a Screen card when J1 Interview shows 2 of 2 places; protocol L step 'try Screen->Interview through the UI' finds no control, no reason is shown, and hro_refused_put_back scores 0 although the server replay is correctly refused. (b) An app writes one Activity line per bulk move, e.g. 'Rafael Costa moved 3 candidates from Applied to Screen' (rules:110 'every move ... a readable line'); hro_activity fails because each card of the multi-card move lacks its own line. (d) Golden: Tomas's independent context remains on the J2 conversation after sending; Rafael sends, Tomas's SSE refresh marks it read in ~1 s, Rafael's page shows 'Seen' before Aud opens, and hro_seen is scored 0.
suggested_fix: (a) Add to hireops_rules.md 'Shown at once, put back if refused' that a move into a full Interview stays offered (or, if blocked early, says why next to the card), or relax hro_refused_put_back to accept a disabled/omitted option with a visible capacity reason. (b) State in rules section 4 that a several-card move records one line per card with its stages, or let hro_activity accept one line that names every card and its from/to stages. (d) In protocol U, tell the judge to close Tomas's context (or move his page off that conversation) before Rafael sends, and to state for Mei whether her page stayed open; then measure hro_seen on the golden in a configured judge run.
